explanations.headline: Never trust browser-supplied prices when creating orders
explanations.rootCause: Your server accepted the order amount directly from the client request instead of looking up the item price in your database. This allowed malicious users to tamper with the price sent in the browser and create a PayPal order for 1 cent.
explanations.impact: Attackers can purchase items for a fraction of a cent, causing direct financial loss to your shop.

fix.code: export async function createOrder(req: Request) {const { productId } = await req.json();const catalogPrices: Record<string, string> = { 'kopi-tee': '25.00' };const itemPrice = catalogPrices[productId];const response = await fetch('https://api-m.sandbox.paypal.com/v2/checkout/orders', {method: 'POST',headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },body: JSON.stringify({intent: 'CAPTURE',purchase_units: [{ amount: { currency_code: 'USD', value: itemPrice } }]})});return response.json();}

explanations.headline: Verify Webhook Signatures to Prevent Forged Orders
explanations.rootCause: The merchant accepted incoming webhook requests without validating their cryptographic signature against PayPal. Because the endpoint lacked verification via the notifications API, any malicious actor who discovered the URL could transmit a fake payload and falsely mark orders as paid.
explanations.impact: Attackers can send forged webhook payloads to mark unpaid orders as fulfilled, causing inventory loss and financial fraud.

explanations.headline: Capture approved orders and check status before fulfilling
explanations.rootCause: The merchant treated an APPROVED order as successfully paid without executing the orders capture API call. Consequently, orders with a status of APPROVED were fulfilled without ever transferring funds.
explanations.impact: You ship goods for payments that never arrived, resulting in direct financial loss.

citations.title: Orders v2: capture payment for order

explanations.headline: Prevent duplicate fulfillment by implementing webhook idempotency checks
explanations.rootCause: The merchant webhook handler processes incoming events without checking if the event ID has already been handled. Because PayPal retries undelivered events, duplicate deliveries trigger multiple shipments for a single payment.
explanations.impact: The shop incurs financial losses by shipping physical goods twice for a single captured payment.

explanations.headline: Handle PAYMENT.CAPTURE.REFUNDED webhooks to keep order status updated
explanations.rootCause: The merchant's webhook endpoint fails to listen for the PAYMENT.CAPTURE.REFUNDED event. When a refund is initiated directly from the PayPal dashboard, the server misses the notification and leaves the local order status marked as paid.
explanations.impact: Your books and inventory system continue to show orders as paid for money you have already refunded, leading to financial discrepancies.
